passages.title: The Science of Sleep
passages.body:
Sleep is far from a passive state. During the night, the brain cycles through distinct stages, each serving a different function. In deep slow-wave sleep, the body repairs tissue and consolidates factual memories. In rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, the brain processes emotions and strengthens procedural skills, such as learning to play an instrument.

Researchers have found that even a single night of poor sleep can impair attention, decision-making, and mood. Chronic sleep deprivation is associated with more serious risks, including weakened immunity and metabolic disorders. Yet modern lifestyles, with their artificial light and constant connectivity, increasingly disrupt natural sleep rhythms.

Interventions need not be complex. Studies suggest that maintaining a consistent sleep schedule, limiting screen exposure before bed, and keeping bedrooms cool and dark can markedly improve sleep quality. Crucially, sleep should be treated not as a luxury but as a biological necessity.
